overview: This single-page Department of State “List of Papers” indexes correspondence filed under “Territory. Kwantung.” The entries span 1930–1937 and refer to diplomatic telegrams from Japan and China, Treasury Department inquiries concerning the correct official designation and political status of Dairen (modern Dalian) in the Kwantung Leased Territory, and correspondence with the New York firm Barnes, Richardson & Colburn. Several entries direct researchers to related material filed elsewhere in the State Department decimal file rather than reproducing the underlying documents.

subfiles.title: Department of State list of papers concerning the Kwantung Leased Territory
subfiles.about: An index records and cross-references diplomatic and Treasury correspondence about the Kwantung Leased Territory and the official name and political status of Dairen.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists papers dated from 1930 through 1937, including communications associated with William R. Castle Jr. in Japan and Nelson T. Johnson in China. It notes Treasury Department inquiries about the country officially encompassing the port of Dairen and about the port’s political status in 1935, together with related correspondence from Barnes, Richardson & Colburn of New York. Some items are represented only by references to other State Department decimal-file locations, including files concerning information, Manchuria, and official nomenclature.

interest: The sheet is useful chiefly as a finding aid: it reconstructs links among diplomatic, Treasury, and private commercial inquiries that were dispersed across several decimal-file classifications. The variant forms “Dairan” and “Darien” also illustrate inconsistent contemporary romanization of Dalian. Most significantly, the indexed questions about what country included the port and its political status expose the practical administrative uncertainty created by Japanese control of the Kwantung Leased Territory and Manchuria during the 1930s.
